# Copilot Instructions

## Project
RAG Showcase: a multi-user document assistant (hybrid search + cited answers) built with Python 3.12, FastAPI, Streamlit, PostgreSQL/pgvector, sentence-transformers and Azure OpenAI (Ollama locally). Current release v0.1.0 (pre-release; versioning restarted on 2026-11-27, all older tags and GitHub releases were deleted); `main` is kept stable (PR required). Users connect their own Dropbox or Google Drive (read-only; one provider and one folder per user) in the UI.

## Layout (package refactor, Nov 2026)
- `app/` API; `app/config.py` holds `MODEL_NAME` / `EMBEDDING_DIMENSION` (single source; imported by search, chunking, embedding, Dockerfile model bake).
- `ui/` Streamlit: `chat.py` (pages), `helpers.py` (Streamlit-free, tested), `start.py` (writes `~/.streamlit/secrets.toml`, sets `PYTHONPATH` to the repo root, execs `python -m streamlit run ui/chat.py`).
- `ingestion/`: `sync_worker.py` (per-user Dropbox sync job), `embed.py` (`embed_pending`), `sample_data.py` (data/sample loader, unowned data).
- `ops/`: `init_db.py` (runs at import, no `main`), `setup_runtime_role.py`, `migrate_job.py` (runs `-m ops.init_db` / `-m ops.setup_runtime_role` with `cwd` = repo root), `manage_users.py`, `idle_stop.py`.
- `connectors/`: sources, extraction, OCR, `chunking.py` (also `split_page`, `split_paragraphs`, `PDF_CHUNKING_VERSION` = `page-token-window-v1`; changing version strings re-chunks documents).
- Run locally as modules from the repo root (`python -m ops.init_db`). Azure commands use file paths (`python ops/idle_stop.py`, `ingestion/sync_worker.py`, `ops/manage_users.py`, `ops/migrate_job.py`, `ui/start.py`) because `az ... --args` mis-parses values starting with `-`; the image sets `PYTHONPATH=/app` so these files can import the packages.
- The root compatibility shims (`ui_start.py`, `sync_worker.py`, `idle_stop.py`, `manage_users.py`, `migrate_job.py`) were removed on 2026-11-27 after every Azure app/job had been moved to the package paths (checked with `az containerapp job list`). `tests/test_deploy_script.py` checks that every command path in the deploy scripts/compose exists and is copied into the image. Only the dead legacy job `rag-ingest` (`python ingest_job.py`) still exists in Azure.
- Removed as unused in multi-user mode (git history has them): single-user Azure ingest job (`ingest_job.py`, `ingest_remote.py`, `azure-ingest-job.*`), `diagnose.py` + workflow, reset scripts/workflow, local PDF pipeline, `search_documents.py`, `evaluation/`, `run_ui.sh`, `test_db_connection.py`. The deployed `rag-ingest` job (if it still exists) has no code any more; delete it.

## Setup & commands (Windows / PowerShell)
- Virtualenv lives in `.venv` (git-ignored): `.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1`
- Install: `pip install -r requirements-dev.txt` (adds pytest); runtime-only deps are in `requirements.txt`.
- Azure deployment: `pwsh ./deploy/azure.ps1 -SubscriptionId <id> -Suffix <x> [-PreflightOnly]` (see `docs/deployment.md`; resumable: detects existing resources and reuses credentials); the image is built by `.github/workflows/build-and-deploy-image.yml` (tags: full commit SHA, `latest` only from `main`).
- Database (`compose.yaml`): `docker compose up -d db` (pgvector/pg16, db/user `rag`, port 5432). Full stack: `docker compose up` (db + api + Streamlit ui on :8501, UI command `python ui/start.py`).
- API: `uvicorn app.main:app --reload`; UI: `python -m ui.start` (needs the Microsoft login variables).
- Tests: `pytest` (`pyproject.toml`: `testpaths = tests`, `pythonpath = .`); single test: `pytest tests/test_api.py::test_health -q`. Full suite takes ~6 min (model loading).
  - `tests/test_api.py` is an integration test: needs a running, indexed Postgres (`DATABASE_URL`) and downloads the embedding model on first run; without a DB it fails/errors (expected).
  - `tests/test_generation.py` mocks Ollama by monkeypatching `httpx.post`; no services needed.
- Lint: `ruff check .` (Ruff defaults, no Ruff config). `ruff format --check .` is not clean repo-wide (pre-existing); don't mass-reformat.

## Architecture
The sync worker and the API share one Postgres database.

**Ingestion:**
- `ops/init_db.py` applies every `sql/*.sql` file in name order (`000_extensions.sql` creates the `vector` extension).
- `ingestion/sync_worker.py` syncs a user's Dropbox folder through `connectors/` (`base.py` types, `dropbox_source.py` REST source on httpx, `limits.py` `files_per_sync`, `chunking.py`, `store.py` Postgres access, `sync.py` change tracking). Re-ingests only files whose remote revision (`documents.source_version`) changed or `failed`; vanished files get `ingestion_status = 'removed'` and no chunks. `PermanentDocumentError` (no text, encrypted, empty, too small) marks a file `unsupported` (`sql/004_unsupported_status.sql`) keeping `source_version`, so it is skipped until the revision changes; transient errors stay `failed` and are retried. File types (`connectors/base.py` `classify`): pdf, txt, md, docx/xlsx/pptx (`connectors/extract.py`), and images + text-less PDFs via Azure Document Intelligence prebuilt-read REST (`connectors/ocr.py`; only when `DOCINTEL_ENDPOINT` + `DOCINTEL_KEY` are set; page budget `DOCINTEL_MAX_PAGES` per run, default 1000; images under `DOCINTEL_MIN_IMAGE_PIXELS` (default 100) fail as "too small" without an API call).
- `ingestion/embed.py` embeds chunks without a current embedding (`embedding_model = MODEL_NAME`, columns from `sql/005_multi_user.sql`, `vector(384)`) and marks documents `indexed`.

**Serving (`app/`):**
- `main.py` – routes `/health`, `/ready`, `/search`, `/chat`. The SentenceTransformer is loaded once in `lifespan` onto `app.state` and retrieval is serialized by `search_lock`. Handlers are sync `def`; error mapping: `ValueError`→422, DB errors→503, `GenerationError`→502.
- `search.py` – embeds the question (normalized; rejects input over the model's token limit) and runs a hybrid search: cosine search (`<=>`), a keyword search (`to_tsvector('simple', text)`, GIN index from `sql/003_hybrid_search.sql`, OR of the question's non-stopword terms) and a file-name/folder-path match (`title ILIKE` plus the Dropbox folder path taken from `source_url`; first 2 chunks of documents ranked by matched terms, name counts double; Google Drive has no folder path), fused by weighted reciprocal rank fusion (`fuse`, name/path leg weight `TITLE_WEIGHT` = 3). `similarity` is always the cosine value. All legs join `chunks` to `documents`, restricted to `embedding_model = MODEL_NAME` and `ingestion_status = 'indexed'`. Changing `MODEL_NAME` (`app/config.py`) requires re-running `python -m ingestion.embed`.
- `generation.py` – provider chosen by `GENERATION_PROVIDER` (`ollama` default, `azure_openai`); both return JSON validated as `GeneratedAnswer`; passages are treated as untrusted. Citations are validated: `citation_ids` must be a non-empty subset of the supplied `S<n>` IDs and include every inline `[S<n>]`, otherwise `GenerationError`. Insufficient evidence returns no citations.
- `db.py` – `get_connection()` opens a new psycopg connection per call from `DATABASE_URL` (no pool); callers using vectors must `register_vector(conn)`. If the connection fails and `POSTGRES_RESOURCE_ID` is set (Azure auto-stop), it asks `app/wake.py` to start the stopped PostgreSQL server (via `app/azure_arm.py`, managed identity) and raises `DatabaseStarting`, which the routes map to 503 "database is starting". `ops/idle_stop.py` (scheduled Container Apps Job, set up by `deploy/azure-autostop.ps1`) stops the server after `IDLE_MINUTES` without API requests.

## Configuration
Env / `.env` (loaded in `app/db.py`): `DATABASE_URL`, `GENERATION_PROVIDER`, `OLLAMA_BASE_URL` (default `http://127.0.0.1:11434`), `OLLAMA_MODEL` (default `llama3.2:3b`), `AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT` / `_DEPLOYMENT` / `_API_KEY` / `_API_VERSION`, connector credentials (ingestion only): `DROPBOX_APP_KEY` / `_APP_SECRET` / `_REFRESH_TOKEN`, `GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON` or `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` / `_CLIENT_SECRET` / `_REFRESH_TOKEN`, `API_KEY` (optional `X-API-Key` check on the user endpoints), `USER_TOKEN_SECRET`, `TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, `DROPBOX_REDIRECT_URI`, `AUTH_REDIRECT_URI`/`AUTH_COOKIE_SECRET`/`MS_CLIENT_ID`/`MS_CLIENT_SECRET`/`MS_TENANT` (UI login), `OWNER_EMAIL`/`ADMIN_DATABASE_URL` (ops/init_db), `RAG_API_BASE_URL` (for `ui/chat.py`), `ACS_EMAIL_CONNECTION_STRING`/`ACS_EMAIL_SENDER`/`UI_BASE_URL` (optional admin e-mails about access requests). In Docker the API reaches host Ollama via `host.docker.internal`.

## Conventions
- Use type hints and Pydantic models for request/response schemas.
- Keep route handlers thin; put logic in separate modules under `app/`.
- Prefer `async def` for handlers that do I/O (new handlers); keep Ruff-sorted imports.
- Add a pytest test (using FastAPI `TestClient`) for each new endpoint.
- Add dependencies to `requirements.txt` (fully pinned).

## Multi-user mode (deployed)
- Schema `sql/005_multi_user.sql`: `users`, `dropbox_credentials` (superseded by `storage_credentials`, `sql/007_storage_providers.sql`, which moves the rows on every run; code no longer uses the old table), `oauth_states` (+ `provider`), `sync_jobs`, `chat_usage`, `audit_log`; `user_id` on `source_connections`/`documents`/`chunks` (trigger-inherited from the parent); RLS policy `owner_only` using `app_user_id()` (setting `app.user_id`, set by `get_connection(user_id)`). RLS is bypassed by the owner/admin role: API and worker must use the `rag_runtime` role (`ops/setup_runtime_role.py`, `RUNTIME_DB_PASSWORD`); migrations use `ADMIN_DATABASE_URL`. `search.py` also filters `c.user_id`.
- Auth: Streamlit `st.login("microsoft")` (`ui/start.py` writes `secrets.toml`; `MS_TENANT` default `consumers` because `common`/`organizations` fail with `invalid_claim: iss`, streamlit#11391). UI signs claims (`USER_TOKEN_SECRET`, 5 min) -> API `current_identity` (verified claims, no allowlist) -> `current_user` -> `users.authenticate` (personal tenant binds by e-mail once; work accounts only via `ops/manage_users.py invite --tid --oid`) -> `current_admin` (`users.is_admin`). The UI loads `/me` once per session (`st.session_state.account`); a 403 shows the access-request page.
- Invite link / access requests (`sql/006_access_requests.sql`, `app/access.py`, admin page in `ui/chat.py`): one shared code in `app_settings` (`<ui>/?invite=<code>`); Streamlit's sign-in always redirects to `/` and drops query params (checked in `streamlit/web/server/starlette/starlette_auth_routes.py`), so the UI stores the validated code in a 1-hour `rag_invite` cookie via `st.html(..., unsafe_allow_javascript=True)` and reads it back with `st.context.cookies` (pasting the link also works). `rag_runtime` has no grants on `access_requests`/`app_settings`; only `SECURITY DEFINER` functions (search_path pinned, EXECUTE revoked from PUBLIC) with `require_admin()` checking `app.user_id`. Approval binds tid+oid; an existing e-mail is only bound for an unbound personal-account invitation, otherwise `email_in_use`. Refused -> 7-day cooldown; max 50 pending. E-mail to admins via `app/notify.py` (ACS e-mail REST, HMAC access-key signing, no SDK; `ACS_EMAIL_CONNECTION_STRING`, `ACS_EMAIL_SENDER`, `UI_BASE_URL`; FastAPI `BackgroundTasks`; logs counts only). `ops/init_db.py` makes `OWNER_EMAIL` admin; `ops/manage_users.py admin|unadmin`.
- Storage per user (Nov 2026): `app/storage.py` (provider-neutral: OAuth state with provider, `storage_credentials` row = one provider + one folder, `set_folder`, `disconnect`, `status`), `app/dropbox_oauth.py` / `app/gdrive_oauth.py` (same interface: `configured`, `authorize_url`, `exchange_code`, `resolve_folder`, `source_for`, `revoke`), shared `app/oauth.py` (`OAuthError`, PKCE). API `/storage/{provider}/authorize`, `/storage/callback`, `/storage/folder`, `DELETE /storage`; `/me` returns `storage` (incl. `available` providers). Switching provider/folder deletes the other cloud `source_connections` (never `local`) only with `confirm_delete`, else `ConfirmationRequired` -> 409. Google: scopes `openid email drive.readonly`, `access_type=offline`, `prompt=consent`; granted scopes are checked (users can untick Drive); account e-mail read from the token-endpoint `id_token`; folder from a pasted link (`connectors/gdrive_source.parse_folder_id`); `GoogleDriveSource.for_user` refreshes the access token on 401. `drive.readonly` is restricted: unverified production app = warning screen + 100-user cap; Testing = 7-day refresh tokens; `drive.file` + Picker does not grant folder children. Env `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`/`_SECRET`/`GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI` (API; worker needs ID+secret), set by `azure-multiuser.ps1` when both are given. Schema releases: run Azure multi-user setup (migration) before approving the image deploy. Tests: `tests/test_multi_user_db.py` covers flow, switch deletion, migration, RLS (16 pass with pgserver). `status()` also lists indexed folders from `source_connections` (legacy owner data has documents but no credentials row, so "connected" is false for it). Chat citations carry the passage `text`; the UI groups sources per document (Streamlit-free helpers incl. the cold-start `request_with_retry` live in `ui/helpers.py`, tested in `tests/test_ui_helpers.py`) and `GET /documents/{id}/chunks` (`app/documents.py`) feeds the passage viewer (extracted text, not the original file: Dropbox cannot be embedded and highlighting inside a PDF would need a PDF renderer). Sync via `app/jobs.py` queue + `ingestion/sync_worker.py` (logs counts only; `connectors/limits.py` rejects folders over `files_per_sync`); API triggers the worker job through `WORKER_JOB_RESOURCE_ID` (ARM) to avoid a polling worker waking the DB.
- `ops/init_db.py` with `OWNER_EMAIL` assigns legacy unowned data to that user and makes them admin (verified idempotent). `APP_PASSWORD` removed.
- Tests: `tests/test_multi_user_units.py` (no services), `tests/test_multi_user_db.py` (needs `TEST_DATABASE_URL`, an admin URL of a disposable server; verified with `pgserver` embedded Postgres 16 + pgvector in a temp venv: `pgserver.get_server(dir).get_uri()`; on slow machines pgserver's hard-coded 10 s `pg_ctl` start timeout fails, wrap `pgserver.postgres_server.pg_ctl` to pass `timeout=180`), `tests/test_api.py` (needs indexed DB + admin `DATABASE_URL`). `ui/chat.py` itself is not unit-tested (Streamlit at import); keep testable logic in `ui/helpers.py`.
- Azure: `deploy/azure-multiuser.ps1` (+ workflow `azure-multiuser.yml`) upgrades an existing deployment: jobs `rag-migrate`/`rag-sync`/`rag-admin`, API on `db-runtime-url` (`rag_runtime`), UI `python ui/start.py`; migration runs before the apps are switched; secrets in `.env.azure.v2`. Full apply verified on Azure (commit `d9098c1`); owner is `adranale@outlook.de` (renamed from the non-Microsoft `adranale@me.com`), legacy data folder `/Unterlagen`. `-EmailNotifications` (workflow input `email_notifications`) creates ACS `acs-email-<suffix>` (Azure-managed domain) + `acs-rag-<suffix>` through `az rest` ARM calls (api-version 2023-04-01, no az extension) and sets the rag-api secret `acs-email-connection`; the `Microsoft.Communication` provider must be registered once by a subscription owner (CI SP has only Reader on the subscription). The sample-data workflows use the admin URL and produce unowned data in multi-user mode. Ad-hoc SQL on Azure: start `rag-admin` with `--image <same image> --command python "--args=-c<code>" --env-vars DATABASE_URL=secretref:db-url` (base64-exec the script; the `-c` must be glued to the code, `az` otherwise mis-parses), then read `ContainerAppConsoleLogs_CL` via `az rest` POST to the workspace `api/query` (ARM).
- Incident (fixed 2026-11-27): the #65 image (Google Drive, needs `sql/007_storage_providers.sql`) was deployed on 2026-11-25 before the migration ran; `rag-api` failed every account call with `UndefinedTable: relation "storage_credentials"` -> UI "API error 503: Account is temporarily unavailable". Fix: Azure multi-user setup workflow with `image_sha`, `preflight_only=false`, `run_migration=true` (migrates first, then switches apps/jobs). Schema releases must run that workflow before approving the image deploy.
- Incident (fixed 2026-11-24): from 2026-11-22 23:10 UTC the managed identities of `rag-api` and `rag-idle-stop` had lost `Contributor` on `pg-rag-ragdemo01` (cause not found; activity-log query failed). Symptoms: every `rag-idle-stop` run `Failed` with `403` on `.../flexibleServers/<name>/stop` (fail-closed, server kept running and billing); the API wake-up (`/start`) would also have failed. Fix: re-run `deploy/azure-autostop.ps1` locally (idempotent; also moved the job to `python ops/idle_stop.py`). Check: `az role assignment list --assignee <principalId> --all` for both identities; logs via `az rest` POST `<workspace id>/api/query` (KQL `ContainerAppConsoleLogs_CL | where ContainerGroupName_s startswith "rag-idle-stop"`; avoid `first`/`last` as column names, they cause `SyntaxError`). Local `az` may default to another subscription (`got-analytics-prd`): always pass `--subscription`.
- Gaps: Key Vault not used; operator can read data; Dropbox dev-mode user cap unverified.

## Azure test deployment task (branch `azure-deployment`)
Goal: a small, sample-data-only Azure deployment of the existing app, run from macOS (PowerShell 7, Azure CLI logged in). Keep PostgreSQL + pgvector; do not redesign the app, migrate the DB, or add LangChain/other vector DBs/private networking. Inspect actual files first, then implement and validate (not just recommend). Do not provision billable resources, change cloud config, push, publish images, or delete anything without explicit approval; stop before executing the deployment. Never print or commit credentials.

Target (defaults in `deploy/azure.ps1`): resource group `rg-rag-showcase`; PostgreSQL 16 Flexible Server (`Standard_B1ms`, 32 GiB, db `rag`, `VECTOR` in `azure.extensions`); Azure OpenAI `gpt-4.1-mini` / `2025-04-14` / `GlobalStandard`; region `francecentral` (westeurope is PostgreSQL-restricted and swedencentral cannot create PostgreSQL on this subscription; gpt-4o-mini has no quota in francecentral); Container Apps env; internal API app (8000, 1 CPU/2 GiB, 0–1 replicas); public Streamlit UI (8501, 0.5 CPU/1 GiB, 0–1 replicas, UI password); shared API key; image `ghcr.io/adranale/rag-showcase:latest`. These defaults are not verified for region availability, quota or cost.

Required work:
1. **Safe errors:** replace `Invoke-Az` (it echoes args incl. secrets on failure) with a helper using a safe operation label, stopping on failure, applied to all `az` calls (also endpoint/key/FQDN lookups); reject empty/invalid required outputs.
2. **Container startup args:** verify the UI `--command python --args=-m,streamlit,...` syntax under PowerShell→az; use a reliable array or YAML config for `python -m streamlit run chat_ui.py --server.address=0.0.0.0 --server.port=8501 --server.headless=true`. Check image contents, workdir, Docker `ENTRYPOINT`/`CMD` (default must serve FastAPI on 0.0.0.0:8000), UI→internal API HTTPS reachability, and that `APP_PASSWORD`/`API_KEY` are really enforced in code.
3. **Generated secrets:** persist before later failures (macOS-safe paths, `.env.azure` git-ignored, restrictive file permissions, never silently overwrite). Don't claim idempotency unless real; either support safe reruns or detect existing resources and stop with recovery steps; avoid rotating DB credentials / mismatching app secrets.
4. **Explicit subscription:** mandatory parameter; resolve, verify enabled, show name/ID/tenant/resource group/region before creating anything; pass it to every command; fail safely. Don't infer NGO funding from the name (billing must be checked separately). An older Free Trial subscription exists and must not be used by accident.
5. **Preflight (before billable steps):** tools and PowerShell version, auth/subscription, az extensions and resource providers, image accessibility and platform compatibility, OpenAI model/version/SKU availability and quota where queryable, naming rules, non-empty UI password. Report what needs manual verification; never silently switch model, region or SKU.
6. **Image publishing:** confirm the workflow builds the intended branch, GHCR permissions, target platform, and that the deployed reference matches the build. Prefer immutable commit tag/digest (configurable) over `latest`; document that anonymous pulls need public package visibility (or implement authenticated pulls). No secrets in the image.
7. **Networking/DB security (document honestly):** `--public-access 0.0.0.0` is the allow-Azure-services exception, not a subscription/app restriction; keep TLS required; validate and restrict the local ingestion firewall rule to the current public IP and document removing it; not production-hardened. Review admin-account use; prefer a least-privilege runtime role if practical, else document the limitation.
8. **Cost wording:** model quota/capacity is not a monetary cap; budget alerts only notify; scale-to-zero ≠ zero idle cost (PostgreSQL, storage, logs); check NGO credit coverage/balance/expiry in billing. No invented price estimates.
9. **macOS ingestion docs:** PowerShell 7 flow to run the script from repo root, load `DATABASE_URL` from the generated file without printing it, create a Python 3.12 venv, install deps, run `python init_db.py`, `python ingest_text.py`, `python embed_chunks.py` (verify schema creates the real `vector` extension). Sample data only; no PDF ingestion or `reindex_all.sh`.
10. **Validation/cleanup docs:** verify `/health`, `/ready`, UI login, UI→API connectivity, sample retrieval, answer generation (API is internal, so no public `curl`; document an internal test method). Document cleanup for the exact resource group with a data-loss warning; never run it automatically.

Validation without deploying: parse the PowerShell script, run tests, validate workflow/config syntax, build/inspect the container if practical, add focused tests; report tested / failed / untestable. Deliver: changed-files summary with reasons, remaining limitations and manual Azure checks, exact macOS commands separated into safe local/preflight vs billable.

## Working agreement
- If a request is ambiguous, ask the user (ask_user) before acting; do not guess and implement.
- Do not commit, push, deploy, or delete anything without explicit approval.
- Update documentation affected by a change (README, instructions) as part of that change; never ask for permission to do so.
- Docs layout: `README.md` stays short (intro, how to try via invite link, stack, how it works, local run); details live in `docs/multi-user.md` (isolation, login, invites, API, limitations), `docs/ingestion.md` (CLI/local/Dropbox/Drive ingestion, OCR, legacy Azure ingest job) and `docs/deployment.md` (Azure base deployment, multi-user upgrade, auto-stop, security, cost, cleanup). Scripts reference these files, not README sections.

### Commit messages
- Commit messages must not mention Copilot or AI tools: no "Co-authored-by: Copilot" trailer, no tool names.

## Security
- Dependabot (`.github/dependabot.yml`: pip, GitHub Actions, Docker; weekly) opens update PRs; Dependabot alerts/security updates are repo settings. `main` is protected (PR required, no force-push/deletion; admins may bypass). Review and merge Dependabot PRs manually, then rebuild/redeploy the image. There is no CI test run on PRs: single pip bumps often do not resolve against the fully pinned `requirements.txt` (check with `pip install --dry-run --ignore-installed --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu -r requirements.txt`; full check = fresh venv in `%TEMP%` + `pytest`). `opentelemetry-*` is its own Dependabot group (lockstep pins); `mpmath>=1.4` is ignored (sympy 1.14 caps it). Nov 2026 cleanup: Dependabot pip PRs #55–#59 were replaced by one tested update PR; branches of merged/superseded PRs and the `review/ocr-and-later` stack (PRs #7–#9, dropped from `main`, superseded by #13/#61) were deleted, SHAs recorded in the session; the repo does not auto-delete head branches.
- Never commit secrets. API keys and OAuth credentials (Google, Dropbox, LLM providers) come from environment variables / `.env` (git-ignored).
- CI hardening: third-party actions are pinned to commit SHAs (`@<sha> # vN`; Dependabot updates them). Workflow logs of this public repo are readable by any GitHub user, so never print file names/paths/titles there: the legacy ingest folder was the `azure-test` secret `INGEST_FOLDER` (masked, no input; removed from the environment together with `DROPBOX_REFRESH_TOKEN` and `RAG_UI_PASSWORD` after the switch to multi-user mode). Workflows left (Nov 2026): `build-and-deploy-image.yml` and `azure-multiuser.yml`; `deploy-azure.yml`, `ingest-sample-data.yml` and `destroy-azure.yml` were removed (provisioning, auto-stop and teardown run locally). The `azure-test` environment only deploys from `main` (custom branch policy + required reviewer). The CI service principal `rag-showcase-github` (object ID `4dc4ee83-…`; use the object ID, not the app ID, for role assignments) has Contributor + RBAC Administrator on `rg-rag-showcase` and Reader on the subscription only; a first-time deployment (provider registration, probe resource group) therefore needs an owner running `deploy/azure.ps1` locally. `az role assignment delete --assignee … --scope <sub>` can remove more than intended: verify with the REST list afterwards.
- Do not log document contents or access tokens.
- Request only the minimum OAuth scopes (read-only where possible).
